question.stem:
All objects uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket must be encrypted for security compliance. The bucket will use server-side encryption with Amazon S3-Managed encryption keys (SSE-S3) to encrypt data using 256-bit Advanced Encryption Standard (AES-256) block cipher.
Which of the following request headers must be used?
question.explanation: SSE-S3 is requested with the single header `x-amz-server-side-encryption: AES256` (for SSE-KMS the value is `aws:kms`, optionally with `x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id`). The three `-customer-*` headers belong to SSE-C, where the client supplies its own key on every request: `-customer-algorithm` (AES256), `-customer-key` (base64 key) and `-customer-key-MD5` (integrity check of the key). Note: since 2023 S3 applies SSE-S3 by default to all new objects, but the header is still how a request explicitly asks for it (and what a bucket policy can enforce).

concept: S3 encryption: request headers — SSE-S3 / SSE-KMS vs SSE-C
tests: Knowing which PUT request header selects SSE-S3 versus the SSE-C customer-key headers.
expected: `x-amz-server-side-encryption` with value `AES256`. Triggers: "SSE-S3", "S3-managed keys", "AES-256" → this header; anything with `-customer-` = SSE-C.
why_not: All three `x-amz-server-side-encryption-customer-*` headers are for SSE-C (customer-provided key, algorithm and key MD5), not SSE-S3.
